subject: Peak shaping & burst policy proposal for Orion Cloud Dedicated
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ellison Kline <ek@orioncloud.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Peak shaping details for Dedicated sizing

Hi Ellison —

Thanks for taking the time earlier. To align the Dedicated sizing and burst policy for Orion Cloud I need two quick inputs so we can draft a clean proposal:

1) Typical baseline steady-state GPU concurrency and the magnitude/duration of the spikes (e.g., "3x baseline for 10–30m every night at 00:00 UTC")
2) Any hard constraints for preemption (can't tolerate evictions during X windows) or approved use of preemptible/spot-like backing capacity

If you prefer, drop the raw hourly usage CSV and we'll ingest it into the capacity matrix. We'll use that to propose a reserved baseline + ephemeral / shoulder slabs and an autoscale policy (targets, cooldowns, max-burst multiplier, eviction priority).

Goal: provide a proposed policy by end of week that maps to a clean billing model and a short canary ramp plan.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: capacity_request_template.csv (text/csv)]

From: Ellison Kline <ek@orioncloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@orioncloud.com>
Date: Thu, 22 May 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Peak shaping details for Dedicated sizing

Karthik —

Appreciate the note. Quick answers below and I've attached an hourly dump for the last 30 days.

- Baseline: ~45 concurrent GPU workers (NVIDIA A100 equivalent) during business hours (14:00–02:00 UTC).
- Nightly spike: a batch ETL pushes peak to ~180 concurrent GPUs (roughly 4x baseline) for 18–35 minutes starting at ~00:10 UTC daily.
- Weekly reporting: a heavier job on Tuesdays spikes to ~250 GPUs (5.5x baseline) for ~45 minutes between 02:00–03:00 UTC as they materialize weekly analytics.
- Ramp onboarding: for the first 6 weeks after go-live we expect a linear ramp from baseline to ~2x baseline as more models are routed to Redwood.

Constraints:
- We cannot tolerate forced evictions during the weekly Tuesday reporting window (02:00–03:00 UTC) — those runs must complete. Outside that window some preemption is acceptable if we get a 30s notice and graceful shutdown hooks to checkpoint jobs.

I attached orion_capacity_matrix.csv. Procurement is looped for contract/term questions.

Thanks,
Ellison Kline
VP, Platform Engineering
Orion Cloud
[Attachment: orion_capacity_matrix.csv (text/csv)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 22 May 2025 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Peak shaping details — propose sizing + burst policy

Looping you both to draft the proposal and pricing. Key constraints from Orion: 180–250 GPU spikes, non-eviction window Tue 02:00–03:00 UTC, onboarding ramp 6 weeks.

Proposal outline I'd like to land on (technical + commercial):
- Reserved baseline: guarantee capacity to cover 1.2x observed baseline (54 GPUs) with committed monthly slab.
- Shoulder (ephemeral warm pool): a pre-warmed slab up to 3x baseline (additional ~135 GPUs) with fast attach (30–60s) for typical nightly spikes.
- Burst (on-demand autoscale): up to 5.5x baseline (targets up to 250 GPUs) for short windows (default max continuous burst 60 minutes, extendable by exception), backed by on-demand inventory.
- Eviction policy: strict no-evict during Tue 02:00–03:00; soft-evict elsewhere with 30s SIGTERM and 3 min graceful drain. Priority-based eviction (batch < async inference < online serving).
- Cooldowns/Auto-scale tuning: ramp factor 2x, stabilization window = 120s, scale-in delay = 300s to avoid oscillation.
- Billing: baseline billed at committed rate; shoulder billed at reduced premium; burst billed at on-demand premium with weekly caps and optional burst-credit bucket for emergency spikes.

Risks / asks:
- Need to confirm whether Orion can tolerate preemptible-backed shoulder nodes (saves cost) with warm rehydrate in 45–90s.
- Confirm max continuous burst toleration (they asked for 45 min weekly spike; we propose 60 min default).

Lauren — can you draft the customer-facing proposal (PDF) with two pricing rows (shoulder using preemptible backing vs fully reserved shoulder) and a short canary ramp (2-week canary then full ramp to 6-week onboarding)
Marissa — can you add an ops runbook section: SLOs, metrics to monitor (pod eviction rate, attach latencies, queue backlog), and our fallback (auto-route to smaller model variant / read-only degraded mode).

I'll consolidate and send to Ellison and Procurement.

—Karthik

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ellison Kline <ek@orioncloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@orioncloud.com>
Date: Fri, 23 May 2025 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing & burst policy — proposal attached

Hi Ellison —

Thanks for the data. Attached is a draft proposal (OrionCloud_Redwood_Dedicated_PROPOSAL_v1.pdf) and a compact capacity matrix. Highlights:

1) Sizing and policy (numbers rounded):
   - Reserved baseline: 54 GPUs (committed)
   - Shoulder pool: +120 GPUs (pre-warmed), option A = preemptible-backed (cheaper), option B = reserved-backed (no preemption)
   - Burst cap: up to 250 GPUs (on-demand) with default max continuous burst = 60 minutes

2) Eviction & windows:
   - Tue 02:00–03:00 UTC = hard no-evict (we will mark routes as protected and route to shoulder/reserved only)
   - Outside protected windows, soft-evict with 30s notice and 180s drain

3) Autoscale tuning (defaults, adjustable):
   - Aggressive scale-out: target utilization 65%, ramp factor 2x, stabilization 120s
   - Conservative scale-in: minimum cool-down 300s to prevent flapping

4) Billing model:
   - Reserved baseline = committed monthly at discounted rate
   - Shoulder Option A (preemptible-backed) = 35% discount vs on-demand; can reduce cost but risk 60–90s rehydrate
   - Shoulder Option B (reserved-backed) = higher cost, zero preemption risk
   - Burst = on-demand at published T&Cs; we can include a capped monthly burst-credit bucket on year-1 deals

5) Canary plan:
   - 2-week canary for a single route and 6-week full onboarding (ramp to 2x baseline during onboarding)

Attachments: proposal PDF + capacity matrix. We included a DocuSign link placeholder for terms; we can prepare a version with the Shoulder Option A pricing (cheapest) and Option B (no-preempt).

Next steps requested from you: confirm preferred shoulder option and procurement point-of-contact for contract redlines.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: OrionCloud_Redwood_Dedicated_PROPOSAL_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]
[Attachment: orion_capacity_matrix.csv (text/csv)]

From: Procurement <procurement@orioncloud.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellison Kline <ek@orioncloud.com>
Date: Tue, 27 May 2025 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing & burst policy — procurement redlines

Lauren / Karthik —

Thanks for the proposal. Procurement reviewed and we have three contract items we need clarified before we can sign:

1) Eviction SLAs & credits: define the measurable threshold (e.g., % of jobs preempted during non-protected windows) and the credit formula. We also need assurance on the 30s notice for preemptible-backed shoulder nodes.
2) Max continuous burst: we need explicit language about how extensions beyond 60 minutes are handled and the pricing for extended bursts.
3) Invoice cadence & forecasting: we'd like monthly invoicing with a forecasted monthly cap and an overage mechanism (30-day notice before sustained >150% of forecast triggers a repurchase).

I've attached procurement_redlines_ORC-047.docx with inline comments. We're inclined to accept Shoulder Option A if Redwood can guarantee the stated rehydrate window (45–90s) and provide an emergency burst-credit bucket for the Tuesday weekly reporting (we'll want to limit it to 2x/week without penalty).

Please respond with the redline-aware proposal PDF and a single-sheet summary of eviction SLAs (we can then route to legal).

Regards,
Procurement Team
Orion Cloud
